note: Window agent p1620-p1629 (Phase D). Fixes: the Saadi Saharan corridor kept after 1618; Mosul and Basra left to nobody or to the Safavids after the 1626 keyframes; the Tumed disc over the Ming provinces of Shanxi and Shaanxi; the unresolved Julfar in the Ya'rubid keyframe.

region.text: the Sahara corridor and Niger bend of the 1591-1595 Saadi shape that the 1612 Moroccan shape lacks

events.note: Direct Saadi control of the Sudan ended in 1618: 'Sultan Moulay Zidan relinquished direct control over the Sudan territories in 1618' and 'After 1612, the Pashas who governed the Sudan region were appointed locally by the Arma'; Morocco kept only 'nominal control' (the Timbuktu pashalik stays a vassal, ledger 25). The dossier's own keyframe saadi-sultanate_1612 holds Morocco alone for 1618-1628, but the 1618 vassal event moved only the pashalik and left about 1,600 cells of the Saharan corridor Saadi until the 1629 snap. The corridor goes to no state from 1620 (the first year of this window); p1610-p1619 carries the same land in 1618-1619.

region.text: the Shanxi and Shaanxi cells inside the 200 km Hohhot disc of the Tumed

events.note: The Tumed realm is drawn as a 200 km disc round Hohhot (tumed ledger 0), which spills over the Ming provinces; the Altan Khan page places the Tumed pastures 'north of the border with Shanxi', so those cells were Ming. The ming-dynasty keyframe of 1622 would claim them anyway; this event gives them to the Ming for 1620-1621 as well.

correction.text: the 1626 shape plus Mosul (Ninawa) and Basra, which the Ottomans held while the Safavids held Baghdad and central Iraq

keyframe_overrides.why: Cliopatria's 1626 Ottoman shape keeps north-western Iraq (all 148 Ninawa cells, 297 Iraqi cells) but not Basra or central Iraq; the Safavids, who hold all Iraq outside Baghdad from the ledger's 1625 loss, win the keyframe conflict by the size rule and then their own 1626 shape drops Mosul, so Mosul went to nobody from 1626 (rulings/0 settles the conflict; the union with Ninawa here is redundant but harmless, Basra is the working addition). [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: this first sentence corrected; it said the Ottoman shape leaves out all of Iraq.] The page has the Ottoman army, on 4 July 1626, 'lifted the siege and withdrew to Mosul', and has the Ottoman-Portuguese coalition defeat the Persians in 1624, who 'retreated from Basra'; the Safavid capture was of Baghdad (14 January 1624), Kirkuk and the shrine cities. The pages do not date the recovery of Mosul.

correction.text: the 1626 shape without Basra, where the Persians were beaten back in 1624 (Baghdad, Kirkuk and central Iraq stay Safavid until 1638), plus the whole province of Kandahar, which the ledger gave the Safavids in 1622

keyframe_overrides.why: The Ottoman-Safavid War page: the Ottoman-Portuguese coalition defeated the Persians in 1624, 'who retreated from Basra'; the shape draws Basra (68 cells) as Safavid for 1626-1635. Kandahar: the shape holds only 123 of the province's 197 cells, so the keyframe snap of 1626 turned the other 74 into nobody's land, a grey hole on the Mughal border: they are the city of Kandahar itself and the east of the province, which Cliopatria's 1626 Mughal shape holds; the Mughal keyframe lost them to the Safavids by the size rule and the Safavid snap then dropped them [reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: was described as 'Registan, south of the city']; the Mughal-Safavid war (1622-1623) page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal%E2%80%93Safavid_war_(1622%E2%80%931623)) has 'the city fell on 22 June' 1622, Zamindawar shortly after, and a Mughal envoy in spring 1623 'accepting the loss of Kandahar'; the dossier's ledger 44 and its other keyframes treat the province of Kandahar as one unit.

correction.text: the 1626 shape without the Portuguese strongpoints at Julfar (Ras al Khaimah, to 1633), Sohar (to 1643) and Muscat (to 1650), which the ledger adds in 1633, 1643 and 1650

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's own correction (same text, same radii) does not resolve because the gazetteer has no 'Julfar'. The Julfar page: 'a predecessor settlement to Ras Al Khaimah, today in the United Arab Emirates', so the Ras al Khaymah place stands in for it. Without the correction the size rule gives the Portuguese holdings (Muscat, Sohar) to the smaller Ya'rubid shape from 1625 to 1649.

region.text: north-western Iraq as Cliopatria's 1626 Ottoman shape draws it (Mosul/Ninawa, Duhok, most of Erbil, strips of Kirkuk, Salah ad-Din and Anbar; 297 cells) and Basra

rulings.why: In 1626 the draft still holds Mosul and Basra as Safavid (ottoman-empire ledger 107 gave 'Iraq' away in 1625), but on 4 July 1626 the Ottoman army 'lifted the siege and withdrew to Mosul', and the Persians had 'retreated from Basra' in 1624; the keyframes of the year are corrected the same way (keyframe_overrides/0 and /1). Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: region widened from Ninawa and Basra to all of the Ottoman shape's Iraq. The other 148 cells of the same conflict (Duhok 22, Erbil 46, Anbar 53, Salah ad-Din 16, Kirkuk 9, Sulaymaniyah 1) also went to the Safavids by the size rule and were then dropped by the Safavid 1626 shape, which lacks them, leaving them grey for 1626-1629; the Mosul page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosul) has Persian rule there only as 'a brief break in 1623' and Mosul before 1638 'an offensive platform for Ottoman campaigns into Iraq'.
